Duane ocular motility anomaly, congenital myopathy and severe early scoliosis define the syndrome.
Endemic treponemal skin infection; oral mucosal erosions and ulcers are characteristic diagnostic manifestations. Destructive bone disease is variable and late.
Congenital skeletal myopathy; respiratory failure (28/29) and dysphagia (23/24) arise from respiratory and bulbar muscle weakness without established intrinsic lung or GI injury.
Congenital sensory/autonomic neuropathy with absent pain perception; hyperhidrosis alone does not establish skin damage.
Congenital hearing loss defines syndrome; temporal hypotrichosis and oral/palatal malformations occur in 80-99%; patent ductus arteriosus in 30-79%.
Monocular outward ocular misalignment is a form of strabismus.
Pontocerebellar and anterior horn degeneration define PCH1; skeletal muscle atrophy occurs in 80-99%, optic atrophy/visual loss in 30-79%. Respiratory failure is neuromuscular.
Hypocellular marrow failure with cytopenias; osteopenia, hypothyroidism and sinusitis each occur in only 1/4 patients.
Epiphyseal skeletal dysplasia causing abnormal joints, osteochondritis and early arthrosis.
Inherited retinal and optic disc colobomas with reduced vision and additional ocular abnormalities.
Adipocytic soft-tissue sarcoma typically arising in deep extremity connective tissues; no specific visceral origin is established.
Monogenic diabetes; retinopathy, albuminuria and polyneuropathy represent separately diagnosed diabetic complications.
Renal dysfunction defines this form of secondary parathyroid/mineral dysregulation. Renal osteodystrophy is a separately specified disease subtype.
Hamartomatous lesion of the lip, an oral structure; supplied phenotypes localize the abnormality to the mouth.
Inherited startle-circuit dysfunction causes hypertonia and stiffness. Reported reflux, hiatus hernia and esophagitis are separate conditions rather than direct GI involvement.
Fungal infection directly involving skin or its appendages.
Mantle cell lymphoma occupying the spleen, a blood organ; lymphoma also requires the immune mechanism axis.
Neurodevelopmental injury, hepatic dysfunction and intrinsic NO-related hypertension each occur in 30-79%. Monilethrix (30-79%) omitted for cap; renal insufficiency is <30%.
Intellectual disability (4/4), central hypothyroidism and hypogonadism define the syndrome; atrial septal defect occurs in 1/3, meeting threshold with limited evidence.
Villous epithelial neoplasm arising in the duodenum.
DGAT1 triglyceride synthesis deficiency causes intestinal villous injury and protein-losing enteropathy; hyperlipidemia in 2/2. Immunoglobulin depletion follows enteric protein loss.
Clinically apparent Nipah/Hendra infections commonly cause encephalitis; pneumonitis and respiratory failure occur in roughly >=30%, with substantial variation between outbreaks.
Brain malformations and arthrogryposis define the syndrome; pulmonary hypoplasia occurs in 2/3. Fetal pyelectasis in 2/3 does not establish renal functional damage.
Focal epilepsy syndrome producing characteristic motor seizures during sleep.
